item.title: No more execution attempts on Christa Pike: UN rights chief
item.description: The UN human rights chief and nine independent rights experts on Thursday called on authorities in Tennessee not to pursue any further attempts to execute Christa Pike, saying her case highlights multiple concerns surrounding the death penalty.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Canada urges stronger partnerships as global order faces ‘rupture’
item.description: Canada’s Foreign Minister Anita Anand warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that the international order has entered an era of profound disruption, calling for stronger multilateral cooperation and new partnerships as major powers increasingly turn away from global economic integration.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Cuba warns against ‘law of the jungle’ as Foreign Minister denounces US pressure
item.description: Cuba’s Foreign Minister warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that escalating military and economic pressure in Latin America and the Caribbean was threatening international law, while accusing the United States of intensifying a decades-long campaign to isolate and weaken his country.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti at ‘watershed moment’, Prime Minister tells UN, urging full backing for security force
item.description: Haiti is at a “watershed moment” in its struggle against gang violence and needs sustained international support alongside stronger national security institutions, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé told the UN General Assembly on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haitians can’t wait to return home and vote in elections says Prime Minister
item.description: “There is a people. A people who can wait no longer.  A people waiting to regain security, to return home to work, to send their children to school, and to freely choose their leaders.” Those are the words of the Haitian Prime Minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, who spoke at a special UN meeting on the future of security in Haiti.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Venezuela seeking rebirth after political crisis and devastating earthquakes, President tells UN
item.description: Venezuela is seeking to rebuild after a period of political upheaval and the destruction caused by twin earthquakes earlier this year, Acting President Delcy Rodríguez told world leaders at the United Nations on Wednesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Trump defends military action against Iran, Venezuela, and calls for rebrand of AI
item.description: US President Donald Trump used his address to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday to defend recent military action against Iran, urging countries to maintain economic pressure on Tehran – and declaring that he now faces a choice between making a deal, or taking far more drastic steps.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Diplomacy is the way to address global challenges, Brazil tells General Assembly
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva told the General Assembly on Tuesday that the UN needs to become a “temple of peace” once again, as it confronts one of the most critical periods in its 80-year history.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti: Child malnutrition crisis worsens amid escalating violence
item.description: Haiti is facing a worsening child malnutrition crisis, with an estimated 253,725 children aged 6 to 59 months projected to suffer from acute malnutrition between June 2026 and May 2027, new UN-backed analysis has revealed.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Repression continues in Venezuela in the face of ‘appalling’ human rights violations
item.description: In Venezuela’s El Rodeo maximum security prison, some of those detained for political reasons are subject to forced intubation – and prolonged confinement in a sealed underground cistern.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Back to school in Haiti: ‘Madame, can you stop what the gangs are doing to us?’
item.description: When UNICEF’s Representative in Haiti Geetanjali Narayan stepped into a classroom in Port-au-Prince at the start of the new school year, she asked the children a simple question: What did they most need from the UN children’s agency?
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Central Park adapts to climate change while helping New York stay cool
item.description: In the heart of Manhattan in New York City, the effects of climate change are becoming increasingly visible.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Deadly gang attacks spike in Haiti
item.description: Following a deadly spate of gang attacks on civilians in Haiti and amid reports of illicit weapons slipping into the Caribbean country, the Security Council has called an emergency meeting at 3pm (local time) to hear and discuss the latest developments. UN News app users can follow our coverage here.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Risks of child recruitment by armed groups rise in post-quake Colombia
item.description: The recent earthquake in Colombia could increase the risk of child recruitment by armed groups in Chocó and Valle del Cauca, where thousands of children remain out of school in areas already affected by conflict, the UN warned on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti ramps up the fight against gangs in the capital, but violence spreads elsewhere
item.description: The killings in Kenscoff began late Sunday, when armed men descended on the farming community in the hills overlooking Haiti’s capital, setting homes ablaze and attacking residents. By Monday, bodies lay in the streets and survivors were searching for missing relatives.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Colombia earthquake: 1.2 million need aid as some communities remain out of reach
item.description: Ten days after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, an estimated 1.2 million people need humanitarian assistance, while some communities have still received little or no aid, UN agencies said on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Colombia earthquake: UN ramps up aid for 100,000 people
item.description: The UN is scaling up humanitarian assistance in western Colombia as needs continue to grow following last week’s devastating 7.4-magnitude earthquake, according to the latest update released on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Colombia quake: In Cali’s ruins, an ‘overwhelming sense of humanity’
item.description: In one of the cities hardest hit by the earthquake that struck Colombia, hundreds of people are still waiting for news of missing relatives, friends and neighbours.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN continues scaling up response to earthquake in Colombia
item.description: The UN on Wednesday continued scaling up assistance to areas affected by the deadly earthquake that hit Colombia two days earlier.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: WHO chief voices concern over Trump Administration’s executive order on vaccines
item.description: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) on Wednesday upheld the safety of childhood vaccines in response to a new directive from the White House to overhaul the recommended inoculation schedule.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Colombia earthquake: UN joins national response
item.description: As earthquake rescue efforts across western Colombia continued on Tuesday, UN agencies said that they stood ready to help “with everything we've got”, in coordination with national authorities.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN offers support to Colombia after magnitude 7.4 earthquake kills dozens
item.description: The UN offered its support to Colombia on Monday after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck the west of the country, killing at least 111 people and injuring at least 87, including several children, while leaving others trapped under the rubble and causing landslides and serious damage to homes and infrastructure.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Cuba: Independent experts condemn new US sanctions as humanitarian crisis deepens
item.description: Independent UN human rights experts on Thursday condemned a fresh round of US sanctions against Cuba, calling them an attempt to force change on “a sovereign State through threats and coercion.”
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Wanton, intentional infliction of incredible pain’ by gangs in Haiti
item.description: Gangs in Haiti continue to terrorise communities with the “wanton, intentional infliction of incredible pain” on people who often are just in the wrong place at the wrong time.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Tate brothers’ US extradition case a ‘step towards accountability,’ says independent expert
item.description: An independent UN human rights expert has welcomed ongoing proceedings in the United States to extradite “manosphere” bloggers Andrew and Tristan Tate to the United Kingdom, calling the case an important step towards accountability for serious allegations of violence against women and girls.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Trapped by a Facebook job advert, freed by a stranger in a taxi
item.description: Sofia* was 27, raising her seven-year-old son alone in Venezuela, and running out of options. For years she had distributed personal hygiene products door to door, but as her customers’ finances collapsed, so did her income.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Women do not stop giving birth in an emergency’ – one month after Venezuela quakes
item.description: One month after twin earthquakes rocked Venezuela, thousands of women and girls continue to face difficulty in accessing essential healthcare and protection services, a senior official with the UN reproductive and sexual health agency UNFPA said on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Nicaragua continues to weaken political freedoms, UN warns
item.description: The UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Wednesday condemned new threats from Nicaragua’s co-president Daniel Ortega to hinder civil rights and prevent dissenting individuals and groups from participating in elections.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘I consider it a miracle’: Pregnant woman pulled from post-quake rubble in Venezuela
item.description: When a 12-story apartment building pancaked in La Guaira, Venezuela, following two powerful earthquakes late last month, panic ensued to save people injured or trapped under the rubble.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: LIVE: Haiti endures violence and hunger, but hopes grow for a more secure future
item.description: Haiti’s future success depends on “security, political engagement, and humanitarian action reinforcing each other,” the UN’s most senior official in Haiti has told the UN Security Council which met in New York on Monday to discuss the way forward for the embattled Caribbean island nation.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
